commitResults.messageBody:
The current message utilities do not include a dedicated formatter
for a full student profile.

This makes the view command harder to keep consistent with the rest
of the user-facing output and leaves detail formatting scattered
across the codebase.

This commit adds a `formatStudentDetails` helper in
`src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/Messages.java` to centralize
the formatting logic.

Keeping the formatting in the shared message utility preserves a
single source of truth and makes the view output easier to read
and maintain.

The change is limited to the message formatter and matches the
existing shared utility pattern used elsewhere in the app.

This commit introduces a `view` command that displays the details
of a student selected from the currently shown list.

The current app can list students but does not support opening a
single student's detailed profile, which limits the user flow for
inspection and review.

The change adds `ViewCommand` and the supporting command wiring so
users can request details by index and receive a formatted
student summary.

This keeps the feature aligned with the existing command structure
and makes student detail access consistent with the rest of the
address book flow.

The command parser currently recognizes the existing list of
features but does not route the `view` command to its parser.

This leaves the newly added student detail command unreachable
through the standard CLI entry point.

This commit adds the `ViewCommand` case in
`AddressBookParser` so the command is parsed and executed.

Keeping the command registration in the central parser preserves
the existing command-dispatch structure and makes the feature
available to users.

The app currently routes commands through the parser, but it does
not yet have a dedicated parser for the new `view` command.

This commit adds `ViewCommandParser` so a valid student index is
parsed into a `ViewCommand` and invalid input is reported with the
standard invalid-command format message.

This keeps the feature aligned with the rest of the command
architecture and preserves the existing parsing conventions.

The app now includes a student detail view flow, but the new
command and parser paths are not yet fully exercised by tests.

This commit adds focused JUnit coverage for the `view` command,
its parser, and the shared message formatter so the new behavior
is verified at the command, parser, and output layers.

The coverage keeps validation aligned with the existing test
structure and confirms that valid input succeeds while invalid
input produces the expected error handling.
Add more testing for Studio Group data field

The `find` command currently supports only name-based keyword
matching, but the command flow and parser are being expanded to
also support studio-group filtering.

This commit updates the command and parser to accept predicate
objects more generally and adds the studio-group keyword
predicate used by the `g/` prefix.

This keeps the filtering logic flexible while preserving the
existing name-based behavior and aligning the usage text with the
actual command capabilities.

The `find` command currently accepts name-only search terms, but
the parser does not yet recognize studio-group filters.

This commit updates `FindCommandParser` to tokenize a `g/`
studio-group prefix, validate blank values, and build a combined
predicate when both names and groups are supplied.

This keeps the command behavior consistent with the existing
search flow while extending it to a second filtering criterion.

The `find` command can filter by names, but it does not yet have
a dedicated predicate for studio groups.

This commit adds `StudioGroupContainsKeywordsPredicate` so
students can be matched by studio group as part of the existing
find flow.

The new predicate mirrors the project’s search pattern and keeps
the filtering logic consistent with the other keyword-based
search utilities.

The `find` parser now supports an additional studio-group filter,
but the current tests only cover the original name-based search.

This commit adds coverage for the `g/` prefix and the blank-value
error case so the new parsing behavior is verified alongside the
existing name search tests.

This keeps the test suite aligned with the updated command
behavior and helps protect the new filter from regressions.

Find searches accepted name-only input but rejected studio-group filters when
the g/ prefix appeared before or after a name. This made commands such as
`find Alice g/1A` and `find g/1A Alice` behave inconsistently.

The parser now follows the actual search semantics by splitting input on
whitespace, capturing g/ values wherever they appear, and rejecting blank group
values with the standard invalid-format message. This keeps the command
behavior aligned with the implemented name and studio-group predicates.

The change is intentionally small and explicit: it preserves the existing
name-only and group-only cases while adding the combined filter path without
changing unrelated command parsing.

This update is supported by parser tests covering valid name-only searches,
valid group-only searches, combined name/group filters, and invalid blank g/
values.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find parser group filter tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The find parser tests cover the current search behavior, but they were missing
assertions for group filters and invalid g/ inputs. This leaves the studio-
group flow unverified and makes regressions easy to miss.

Add focused parser tests for valid name-only, group-only, and combined
name/group searches, plus invalid cases such as blank g/ values and
name-after-group ordering.

This keeps validation centered on the actual user-facing command behavior and
avoids changing unrelated parser logic.

The staged change is limited to the affected test file and checks the
behavior expected from the current find command semantics.

The find command only handled name keywords, and studio-group searches
were inconsistent across ordering and validation. Users could enter
group filters in some valid forms but not reliably.

This made the feature difficult to reason about and produced confusing
behavior when a g/ filter was combined with a name search. The parser
needed to follow the intended contract rather than rely on fragile
tokenization.

Update the parser to split input on whitespace, collect name and
studio-group keywords independently, and reject blank g/ values with
the standard invalid-format message. Keep the existing name-only and
group-only behavior intact while supporting the combined case.

This approach matches the implemented predicate logic and keeps the
search behavior explicit and predictable. It also preserves the
expected semantics when both name and group filters are present.

The related parser tests should cover valid and invalid name/group
combinations, and the UI changes in this diff should be committed
separately as their own logical change.

The find command still treats studio-group filters inconsistently. Inputs
such as g/1A and Alice g/1A can be parsed differently depending on where
the prefix appears in the input.

This makes search results unreliable and breaks the expectation that
name-based and studio-group filters work together in a predictable way.
Users also lose the ability to validate invalid g/ input consistently.

Update the tokenizer and parser to recognize g/ prefixes anywhere in
the input, gather name and group keywords separately, and reject blank
group values with the standard invalid-format message.

This matches the actual predicate behavior for name and studio-group
matching, while keeping the parser consistent across valid and invalid
search inputs.

The find command still treats studio-group filters inconsistently depending on where g/ appears in the input.

This makes search results unreliable and breaks the expectation that name and studio-group criteria work together predictably.

Update the tokenizer and parser to recognize g/ prefixes regardless of position, separate name and group keywords, and reject blank group values with the standard invalid-format message.

This matches the implemented predicate behavior and keeps parsing stable across valid and invalid search inputs.

The find feature accepts studio-group filters, but the predicate still compares
raw search strings instead of validated studio groups.

This creates a mismatch between how the parser interprets g/ values and how
the matching logic checks student data, which makes combined name and group
searches harder to reason about.

Convert the studio-group predicate to store and compare StudioGroup objects
instead of raw strings, and keep equality and string output consistent with
that representation.

This keeps the search behavior aligned with the domain model and avoids
invalid or mixed-case group values drifting into the filter logic.
